title: Continuous approximation on a Gaussian torus
statement: Let $n\ge0$, let $\mu$ be a finite measure on $\mathbb R^n$, and let $p$ be an extended nonnegative real number with $1\le p<\infty$. If $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ belongs to $L^p(\mu)$, then there is a sequence of continuous real-valued functions on the torus indexed by $\mathbb N^n\times\{0,1\}$ whose compositions with the map sending $x$ to the torus point with coordinates $x_i$ and $\sqrt2 x_i$ converge to $f$ in $L^p(\mu)$ and converge to $f$ pointwise for $\mu$-almost every $x$.
